                     </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="3">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:290" />3 And he walked in all the sins of his father <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Which his Father lived in, Either, First, Before his hu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />miliation. Or rather, Secondly, After his deliverance from <ns0:hi>Shishak,</ns0:hi> when, though he did not openly renounce the Wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ship of God, he seems to have relapsed into his former sins; which otherwise would not have been remembred against him; as <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s name and memory is never loaded with the shame of his sins, because he truly repented of them.</ns0:note>, which he had done before him: and his <ns0:note place="margin">Chap. 11. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#APEX" extent="1+ letters">
                           <ns0:desc>•…</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> heart was not perfect with the LORD his God, as the heart of David his father.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="4">4 Nevertheless, for Davids sake did the LORD his God give him a <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Or,</ns0:hi> candle.</ns0:note> lamp <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> A Son and Successor to perpetuate his name and memory, which otherwise had gone into obscurity. The same Phrase is used above, <ns0:hi>ch.</ns0:hi> 11. 36. 2 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 8. 19. 2 <ns0:hi>Chr.</ns0:hi> 21. 7.</ns0:note> in Jerusalem, to set up his son after him, and to establish Jerusalem <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> That he might maintain that City, and Tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple, and Worship, as a witness for God, in the World, a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> and Heathen world, who should have en<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quired after it, and embraced the True Religion there esta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />blished and set up, as a <ns0:hi>Beacon</ns0:hi> upon an high Hill, that all men might take notice of it.</ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="5">5 Because David did <ns0:hi>that which was</ns0:hi> right in the eyes of the LORD, and turned not aside from any <ns0:hi>thing</ns0:hi> that he commanded him all the days of his life, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Sam. 11. 4 and 12. 9.</ns0:note> save onely in the matter of Uriah the Hit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tite <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>Quest.</ns0:hi> How is this true, seeing <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> sinned in the mat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter of <ns0:hi>Nabal,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 25. and <ns0:hi>Achish, chap.</ns0:hi> 27. and <ns0:hi>Mephi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bosheth,</ns0:hi> and his indulgence to his Children, <ns0:hi>Adonijah, Am<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />non</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Absalom;</ns0:hi> and in the numbring of the People? <ns0:hi>Ans.</ns0:hi> This and the like Phrases are not to be understood as exclusive of every sinful action, but onely of a sinful course or state, or of an habitual and continued Apostacy from God, or from his ways, as the very Phrase of <ns0:hi>turning aside</ns0:hi> from God or from his Commands, doth constantly imply, as ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pears from <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 32. 8. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 9. 12, 16. 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 8. 3. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 78. 57. <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 44. 20. 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 1. 6. and 5. 15, &c. And thus it is most true. For <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s other sins were either sudden and transient acts, proceeding from humane infirmity, and ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />traordinary temptations, and soon repented of and blotted out, as in the cases of <ns0:hi>Nabal</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Achish;</ns0:hi> or, mistakes of his judgment, which was not fully convinced of the sinful<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness of such actions, as in the other cases alledged: whereas that which concerned <ns0:hi>Uriah</ns0:hi>'s Wife was a designed and studi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ed sin, long continued in, defended with a succession of o<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther sins, presumptuous, and scandalous to his Govern<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment, and to the True Religion, which he so eminently pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fessed.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="6">6 And there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">Which was said, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 14. 30. and may be here repeated to signify the Cause and Original of the War between <ns0:hi>Abi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />jam</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ieroboam,</ns0:hi> which is implied here, and particularly described, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 13. <ns0:hi>Abijam</ns0:hi> continued the War which <ns0:hi>Rehoboam</ns0:hi> had begun, and pushed it on to a decisive Battel. But the place may be thus rendred, <ns0:hi>Yet there was war,</ns0:hi> &c. <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Although God was pleased to shew so much respect to <ns0:hi>David,</ns0:hi> as for his sake to continue the Succession to the Kingdom in his Posterity, yet he thought fit to manifest his displeasure against <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi>'s Successors for their sins, and to mix their honour and happiness with Wars and Troubles.</ns0:note> all the days of his life.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="7">7 Now the rest of the acts of Abijam, and all that he did, <ns0:hi>are</ns0:hi> they not written in the book of<ns0:note place="margin">* 2 Chr. 13. 3.</ns0:note> the chronicles of the kings of Judah <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">In their Annals; whence they were long after this time Translated into the Sacred Book of <ns0:hi>Chronicles.</ns0:hi> See above on <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 14. 19.</ns0:note>? And there was war between Abijam and Jeroboam.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="8">8 And Abijam slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David: and Asa <ns0:note place="margin">2 Chr. 14. 1.</ns0:note> his son reigned in his stead.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="9">9 ¶ And in the twentieth year of Jeroboam <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">In or towards the end of the Year. See above, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 1.</ns0:note> king of Israel, reigned Asa over Judah.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="10">10 And forty and one years reigned he in Jeru<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />salem: and his <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">That is, grand<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mother.</ns0:note> mothers <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> His Grand-Mothers, as appears from <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 2. who is called his <ns0:hi>mother,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> is called <ns0:hi>Abijam</ns0:hi>'s <ns0:hi>father, v.</ns0:hi> 3. and this <ns0:hi>Asa</ns0:hi>'s <ns0:hi>father, ver.</ns0:hi> 11. And so the names of <ns0:hi>father,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>mother,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>sons,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>daughters,</ns0:hi> are oft taken, both in Sacred and Prophane Authors, for Grand-Parents and Grand-Children. And his Grand-Mothers name may be here mentioned, rather than his Mothers, because his Mother was either an obscure person, or was long since dead, or indi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sposed, or unwilling to take care of the Education of her Son, and so he was Educated by the Grand-Mother, who, though she did Poison his Father <ns0:hi>Abijam</ns0:hi> with her Idolatrous Principles, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 12. yet could not infect <ns0:hi>Asa,</ns0:hi> nor with-hold him from prosecuting his good purposes of Reforming Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ligion. Which is here remembred to his praise.</ns0:note> name <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> Maachah, the daughter of Abishalom.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="11">11 And Asa did <ns0:hi>that which was</ns0:hi> right in the eyes of the LORD <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">As to the Government of his Kingdom, and Life, and the Reformation, and Establishment of Gods Worship.</ns0:note>, as <ns0:hi>did</ns0:hi> David his father.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="12">12 And he took away the Sodomites <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">Of whom see <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 14. 24. not all of them, but those whom he could find out; but some escaped his observation and censure, as appears from <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 22. 46.</ns0:note> out of the land, and removed all the idols that his fathers had made.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="13">13 And also <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Chr. 15. 16.</ns0:note> Maachah his mother, even her he removed from <ns0:hi>being</ns0:hi> queen <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> He took from her either the Name and Authority of Queen Regent, which she, having been <ns0:hi>Rehoboam</ns0:hi>'s Wife, and <ns0:hi>Abijam</ns0:hi>'s Mother, took to her self during <ns0:hi>Asa</ns0:hi>'s minori<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty, and abused to the Patronage of Idolatry; or, the Digni<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ty of the Queen-Mother, and those Guards, or other Ensigns of Honour, or Instruments of Power, which, as such, she had enjoyed and misemployed. Otherwise, <ns0:hi>he removed her from the queen,</ns0:hi> i. e. from his Wife, that she might not be infected by her, and afterwards infect his Children: which was a prudent and necessary care<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> for the prevention of so great and publick a Mischief.</ns0:note>, because she had made <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> an hor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ror.</ns0:note> an idol <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">Heb. <ns0:hi>a terror,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>horror,</ns0:hi> i. e. an horrible Idol; which it may be he so called, either, because all Idols, though for a season they please, yet in the end will bring dreadful effects upon their worshippers: or, because this was an Idol of a more horrible or terrible shape, more abominable than ordinary, and not to be seen without hor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ror: whether it was that filthy Idol, called <ns0:hi>Priapus,</ns0:hi> which was commonly placed in Groves or Gardens; or, <ns0:hi>Pan,</ns0:hi> or some other Heathen god, to whose service she in a special manner devoted her self.</ns0:note> in a grove, and Asa <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> cut off.</ns0:note> destroyed her idol, and burnt <ns0:hi>it</ns0:hi> by the brook Kidron <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">That when it was burnt to powder, it might be thrown into the Water, and be unfit for any use. See <ns0:hi>Exod.</ns0:hi> 32. 20. <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 12. 3.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="14">14 But the high places were not removed <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>Obj.</ns0:hi> He did take these away, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 14. 3. <ns0:hi>Ans.</ns0:hi> He took away those which were devoted to the worship of Idols, as is there said, <ns0:hi>he took away the altars of the strange</ns0:hi> gods, <ns0:hi>and the high places,</ns0:hi> to wit, where they were wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />shipped: but as for those high places where the True God was Worshipped, he did not take them away; partly, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause he thought there was no great Evil in them, because they had been used by <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Solomon,</ns0:hi> and other Good and Wise men; and because the True God was there wor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />shipped, and that in the manner, though not in the place, which God had appointed; and partly, because he thought the removal of them might do much more hurt than their continuance, to wit, by occasioning the total neglect of Gods Worship by many of the People, who either could not, or through want of competent Faith and Zeal would not go up to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> to Worship, now especially, when the <ns0:hi>Israelites,</ns0:hi> their near Neighbours, formerly their Friends, were become their Enemies, and watched all opportunities to invade or molest them, which they concluded they would do when all their Males were gone up to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem;</ns0:hi> and partly, because the People were so obstinately bent towards them, that it was, or at least, seemed to him, impossible to remove them without great offence, or such commotions as were highly dangerous to that Church and State.</ns0:note>: nevertheless, Asa his heart was perfect with the LORD <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> He did sincerely and constantly adhere to the Worship and Ser<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vice of God. Though he could not hinder the People from using the high places, yet he did intirely Devote himself to the Worship of God in the manner and place prescribed by God.</ns0:note> all his days.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="15">
                     <ns0:pb facs="tcp:107763:291" />15 And he brought in the <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> holy.</ns0:note> things which his father had dedicated <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>Abijam,</ns0:hi> to wit, when he was in distress, and going to fight with <ns0:hi>Ieroboam,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 13. though afterwards he did not perform his Vows, nor bring in what he had Devoted; whether because he was prevented by Death, or because he afterwards relapsed to Idolatry, as may seem probable from the 12 Verse of this Chapter.</ns0:note>, and the things which him<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />self had dedicated, into the house of the LORD, silver, and gold, and vessels.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="16">16 ¶ And there was war between Asa and Baa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sha king of Israel all their days <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">So long as they two Lived and Reigned together. Which is not so to be understood, as if there were a solemn and declared War continuing all that time (for <ns0:hi>Asa</ns0:hi> was <ns0:hi>quiet</ns0:hi> in a great measure for his first <ns0:hi>ten years,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Chr.</ns0:hi> 14. 1. till the <ns0:hi>Israelites</ns0:hi> had recovered themselves from that dreadful blow given them by <ns0:hi>Abijam,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 13. and <ns0:hi>Baasha</ns0:hi> began to Reign in <ns0:hi>Asa</ns0:hi>'s third Year) but so that there were many pri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vate and particular Hostilities practised among them; in which sense the same Phrase is used, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 14. 30.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="17">17 And <ns0:note place="margin">2 Chr. 16. 1.</ns0:note> Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">Perceiving <ns0:hi>Asa</ns0:hi>'s great success; of which see 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 14<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and 15. and the defection of many of his own Subjects to him, upon that occasion, 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 15. 9. he began to be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stir himself, and commenceth a War against him.</ns0:note>, and built <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">
                        <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> Re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />paired and Fortified.</ns0:note> 
                     <ns0:hi>Ramah</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">A City of <ns0:hi>Benjamin;</ns0:hi> which either belonged to the Kingdom of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> from the division (as some other places of that Tribe are supposed to have done; of which see on 1 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 11. 13.) or belonged to <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> but was now Invaded and taken by <ns0:hi>Baasha,</ns0:hi> and Fortified.</ns0:note>, that he might not suf<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fer any to go out or come in to Asa king of Ju<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dah <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">Therefore he chose this place, because it was in the way from his Kingdom to <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> and, as some add, in, or near the straits of the Mountains, where they could easily discover and hinder all Passengers that way.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="18">18 Then Asa took all the silver, and the gold that <ns0:hi>were</ns0:hi> left <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">These poor remainders, which, either <ns0:hi>Shishak</ns0:hi> had left at that time, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 14. 26. or, <ns0:hi>Abijam,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Asa,</ns0:hi> or others, both of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> had dedicated; which probably was not inconsiderable, because <ns0:hi>Asa</ns0:hi> had got great spoils from <ns0:hi>Zerah,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Chron.</ns0:hi> 14. and he and his numerous and prosperous People did at this time express a great Zeal for the House and Worship of God.</ns0:note> in the treasures of the house of the LORD, and the treasures of the kings house, and delivered them into the hand of his servants: and king Asa sent them to <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Chr. 16. 2.</ns0:note> Benhadad <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">Wherein he committed three great faults, amongst many others, First, he Alienated things Consecrated to God, without necessity. Secondly, He did this out of Carnal fear and distrust of that God whose Power and Goodness he had lately experienced. Thirdly, He did this for an ill intent, to hire him to the breach of his League and Covenant with <ns0:hi>Baasha, v.</ns0:hi> 19. and to take away part of that Land which by Right, and the spe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cial Gift of God, belonged to the <ns0:hi>Israelites.</ns0:hi>
                     </ns0:note> the son of Ta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />brimon, the son of Hezion king of Syria, that dwelt at Damascus, saying,</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="19">19 <ns0:hi>There is</ns0:hi> a league between me and thee, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> between my father and thy father <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">Whereby it appears, that albeit he was an adversary to <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> all <ns0:hi>Solomon</ns0:hi>'s days, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 11. 25. yet after the division of the Kingdoms of <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Iudah,</ns0:hi> he was in League with both of them, either, because his designs lay upon the en<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />largement of his Empire other ways; or rather, because he thought it his Wisdom and Interest to leave them to them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves to undo one another by their intestine Wars, and so to prepare the way to his Conquest of both; whereas his Invading of either of them might have made up the breach, and forced them to unite against their common Enemy. And therefore as soon as he was free from this fear, and one of them needed and earnestly desired his help against the other, he gladly embraced the opportunity.</ns0:note>: behold, I have sent unto thee a present of silver and gold: come, and break thy league with Baasha king of Israel, that he may <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
                        <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> go up.</ns0:note> depart from me <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">That being called to defend himself, he may be forced to depart from my Territories.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="20">20 So Ben-hadad hearkned unto king Asa, and sent the captains of the hosts which he had, against the cities of Israel, and smote Ijon, and Dan, and Abel-beth-maachah, and all Cinneroth <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">The Northern parts of <ns0:hi>Baasha</ns0:hi>'s Kingdom, which were nearest to his own Kingdom of <ns0:hi>Damascus,</ns0:hi> and most remote from those parts where <ns0:hi>Baasha</ns0:hi> was now employed, which were in the most Southern parts of his Dominions.</ns0:note>, with all the land of Naphtali.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="21">21 And it came to pass, when Baasha heard <ns0:hi>thereof,</ns0:hi> that he left off building of Ramah, and dwelt in Tirzah <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Now the Royal City of <ns0:hi>Israel.</ns0:hi> See <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 14. 17. There he abode to defend his own Kingdoms, and durst not return to oppose <ns0:hi>Asa,</ns0:hi> lest the <ns0:hi>Syrian</ns0:hi> King should make a second and worse Invasion. So <ns0:hi>Asa</ns0:hi> met with success in his ungodly course, as on the other side good men sometimes meet with disappointment in a good cause and course. So there is no judging of Causes by Events.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
                  <ns0:p n="22">22 Then king Asa made a proclamation throughout all Judah, (none <ns0:hi>was</ns0:hi> 
                     <ns0:note n="‡" place="margin">
